data.title: Counting Knister Scores
data.statement:
Knister is a dice game played on a 5×5 scorecard. Each round, two six-sided dice are rolled and the player writes their sum (a number from 2 to 12) in an empty cell. After 25 rounds the card is full and gets scored.

The card is scored line by line. There are 12 lines: the 5 rows, the 5 columns and the 2 diagonals. Every cell belongs to several lines; the centre cell even belongs to four.

Each line scores points for the combination formed by its five numbers:

Pair (exactly two equal numbers): 1 point, e.g. 4 5 6 7 5
Two pairs: 3 points, e.g. 5 6 6 10 5
Three of a kind (exactly three equal numbers): 3 points, e.g. 7 8 7 7 4
Full house (three of a kind plus a pair): 8 points, e.g. 4 9 4 4 9
Four of a kind (exactly four equal numbers): 6 points, e.g. 6 3 6 6 6
Five of a kind: 10 points, e.g. 8 8 8 8 8
Straight containing a 7: 8 points, e.g. 7 10 8 6 9
Straight without a 7: 12 points, e.g. 3 5 6 2 4

- A straight is five consecutive numbers, in any order. Four consecutive numbers plus one other number is not a straight.
- <<A line scores exactly one combination>>: the one that describes all five numbers. A full house scores 8, not 3 + 1.
- A line without any of these combinations scores 0.
- <<Points scored on the two diagonals are doubled.>>

(7 is the most likely sum of two dice, so a straight that avoids it is rarer and worth more.)

Output the total score of the scorecard.

Full house (three of a kind plus a pair): 8 points, e.g. 4 9 4 4 9

Input
5 lines: 5 space-separated integers value, one row of the scorecard.
Output
One integer: the total score of the scorecard.
Constraints
2 ≤ value ≤ 12
Example
Input
5 6 9 2 7
3 10 8 10 5
4 5 11 6 10
7 9 4 8 2
12 4 5 7 6
Output
1
